title: Draft: Avoid deep-copying QString in various UI interfaces
description:
These (and others) are flagged by Coverity as involving
inefficient/unnecessary copies.

notes.body: Is it safe to do this?  Not going to make a noticeable performance difference, but it bugs me that these are being copied.

My understanding is that:

1. It's safe
2. Sometimes it can be even better in normal C++ usage to move-construct.
3. However, since QString is a Qt [implicitly shared class](https://doc.qt.io/qt-6/implicit-sharing.html), these are generally shallow copies unless and until the string is changed. ("For this reason, you can pass instances of these classes as arguments to functions by value without concern for the copying overhead.") Coverity doesn't know about the Qt implicit sharing, so it flags them.
4. OTOH, making them const (pointers or not) if we definitely know we never want to change them can prevent accidentally impacting performance at the point of changing them.
Yes, I should have done this search first.  There seems to be little point in explicitly passing as references, but as you say it might be worth adding const where it makes semantic sense.
